notes: Strip f: x 8770-10441 plus overlap from x 8470. Names: Robertson ('ROBERTSON' further west, 'AVE.' here), Leslie ('LESLIE' west, 'AVE'), Ida ('IDA' west, 'AVE.' east of Beech), Marsh ('MARSH' at x~7100, 'AVE.' east of Beech), Melrose ('MELROSE' west, 'AVE.'), Linden ('ST.' at the top, 'LINDEN' at y~2050), Beech ('AVE.' at the top, 'BEECH' at y~2200), Williams ('AVENUE' here, 'WILLIAMS' west), Dacey, Carland, Atlantic ('AVE.'), Edwards ('ROAD' at y~2250 and 'EDWARDS' at y~6200 on the same N-S road along the east edge; 'CITY LIMIT' printed along it). Duck Creek Road: 'DUCK CREEK' printed on the N-S road at x~8290 (strip e) and on the E-W band at y~2810, 'ROAD' on the SSW stretch and 'ROAD 60'' on the ENE stretch near x 10050; treated as one road: north from x~8290, NNE to Williams, east along y~2810, ENE past Beech, curving NNE to Marsh/Edwards and on to the plate edge (the NNE stub past Edwards is unlabelled). Smith Road: 'SMITH' on the NW diagonal near Robertson (x~6900), 'ROAD' near Melrose, and 'ROAD'/'SMITH' on the N-S part south of Williams; one road. Edmonson: 'EDMONSON' on the SE diagonal, 'ROAD' on the ESE stretch near Edwards (continuous); recorded as Edmonson Road. Uncertain: 'MI...' and 'MAR...' east of Edwards (cut by the plate edge), the '...AVE.' stub at the bottom notch, 'WOOD ... ST.' (letters widely spaced, a track runs through the label; read as Wood Street), and whether the bottom band east of Madison is Wood Street. Not streets: Duck Creek (creek), the railroad spurs and the 10-inch-pipe strip at x~8900-8990, the 6-inch-pipe line at x~8745 through the lumber yard, the narrow strip south of the Edmonson-Edwards lots (6-inch pipe), the grey/pink/teal boundary bands, and the dotted boundary at x~10301 north of Marsh. Edmonson's west end at Duck Creek Road (~8292,3778), Duck Creek Road's bend at ~(8292,3717) and Smith Road / Melrose (~8370,2392) lie west of x 8470 and are left to strip e. Madison Road: a second line runs parallel about 55 px NW of the block line on its NW side (one lot line crosses it, Wood Street's north edge stops on it); centre taken midway between the two readings.
